speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Varicella (Chickenpox) secondary to exposure.

The history of a brother with chickenpox one month ago, combined with the daycare exposure, strongly suggests this is a breakthrough varicella infection despite up-to-date immunizations. The lesions are likely in the "dewdrop on a rose petal" stage; I am waiting for the skin images and CBC results to confirm the viral etiology and rule out a bacterial superinfection.
